newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmen Vneshekonombank to seek intl credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen Vneshekonombank to seek intl credit rating.

text.p: Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has told Vneshekonombank, the state-run bank for foreign economic relations, to reach agreements with leading credit rating agencies, Niyazov's press service said on Monday.
A press service official told Reuters that in line with Niyazov's order Vneshekonombank would have to negotiate with U.S. agencies Standard and Poor's and Moody's and Britain's IBCA.
Niyazov's office and Vneshekonombank declined to say whether they needed a credit rating to place Turkmenistan's securities on international financial markets.

In neighbouring Kazakhstan, private Kazkommertsbank was assigned by U.S. rating agency Thomson Bank Watch a B- rating in January. The bank has said it plans to place on international markets Eurobonds worth $100 million.
Kazakhstan's largest state-run Halyk Savings Bank said earlier this month it was also planning to get an international rating to borrow up to $100 million in a Eurobond issue.
